title: iPhone 15 battery replacement
fault: Battery drains too quickly, likely due to worn cell
diagnosis: A battery that drains fast on an iPhone 15 is usually a worn cell, so I'll walk you through replacing it. This is a medium-difficulty repair, so go slowly with the adhesive tabs and the connectors.
safety_notes: Never puncture or bend the battery; if it is swollen or damaged, stop and take it to a repair shop.
Let the battery drain below 25% before starting.
Keep metal tools away from the battery connector.

steps.title: Power off the phone
steps.instruction: Hold the side button and a volume button, then slide to power off. Unplug any cable and remove the case.
steps.expected_visual_state: The screen is completely black, with no cable attached and no case on the phone.
common_mistakes: Only locking the screen instead of fully powering off
Leaving the charging cable plugged in

steps.title: Remove the pentalobe screws
steps.instruction: Use the P2 pentalobe screwdriver to remove the two screws beside the USB-C port. Put them in a dish.
steps.expected_visual_state: Two empty screw holes are visible on the bottom edge next to the USB-C port, and the screws are in a tray.
common_mistakes: Using the wrong screwdriver and stripping the heads

steps.title: Lift the display
steps.instruction: Attach the suction handle near the bottom of the screen and pull gently while sliding a plastic spudger around the edge. Open the display like a book, hinged from the side, and don't pull it past about 90 degrees.
steps.expected_visual_state: The display is lifted and propped open at the side, still attached by its flex cables to the body.
common_mistakes: Prying too hard and cracking the glass
Pulling the display fully away and tearing its flex cables

steps.title: Disconnect the battery connector
steps.instruction: Remove the screws on the display bracket, then the battery connector bracket. Use the spudger to pry the battery connector straight up.
steps.expected_visual_state: The display and battery connector brackets are off and the battery connector is disconnected from the board.
common_mistakes: Disconnecting the battery before removing the brackets
Prying at an angle and bending the connector
Mixing up the different bracket screws

steps.title: Release the battery adhesive
steps.instruction: Peel each of the four stretch-release tabs slowly, pulling them straight and flat along the battery. Lift the battery out when it comes free.
steps.expected_visual_state: The old battery is out of the frame, with the empty battery bay visible and the tabs peeled out.
common_mistakes: Pulling tabs upward so they snap
Prying the battery with a metal tool
Pulling too fast so the tabs break

steps.title: Fit the new battery
steps.instruction: Clean the bay, then press the new battery into place with its adhesive. Plug the connector in and press it down gently.
steps.expected_visual_state: The new battery is sitting flat in the bay with its connector seated and the tabs tucked in.
common_mistakes: Leaving dust or old adhesive under the new battery
Not pressing the connector fully flat

steps.title: Reassemble the phone
steps.instruction: Refit the brackets and display connectors, then close the display. Replace the two pentalobe screws.
steps.expected_visual_state: The display sits flush against the frame with both bottom screws in place.
common_mistakes: Trapping a cable as the display closes

steps.title: Power on and test
steps.instruction: Hold the side button until the Apple logo appears and charge to 100%. Check Settings, Battery, Battery Health for the new capacity.
steps.expected_visual_state: The phone boots to the home screen and the Battery Health screen shows a healthy capacity.
common_mistakes: Judging the result before a full charge cycle
Ignoring a Battery Health message about an unknown part
